issue_context.title: [API Proposal]: `ReadOnlySpan<char>` overloads for `StringNormalizationExtensions`
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-globalization See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Background and motivation If we try to verify that the string represented by `ReadOnlySpan` is Unicode normalized, we currently have to turn it into a `string` once. Overloading for `ReadOnlySpan` is needed to reduce allocation. ### API Proposal ```diff namespace System; public static class StringNormalizationExtensions { + public static bool IsNormalized(this ReadOnlySpan strInput, NormalizationForm normalizationForm = NormalizationForm.FormC); + public static bool TryNormalize(this ReadOnlySpan strInput, Span destination, out int charsWritten, NormalizationForm normalizationForm = NormalizationForm.FormC); } ``` ### API Usage ```csharp ReadOnlySpan partOfhugeArray = hugeArray.AsSpan(start, length); if (!partOfhugeArray.IsNormalized()) throw new Exception("Text must be Unicode normalized."); /// ... ``` ### Alternative Designs _No response_ ### Risks _No response_
Author: udaken
Assignees: -
Labels: `api-suggestion`, `area-System.Globalization`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -
@udaken I made a few edits to the proposal and hope that works for you.

review_comments: The previously commented on charsWritten = 0 also doesn't match with this.
Can the string method above just call this one?

If we assume all characters are normalized, shouldn't we be copying them to the destination and setting charsWritten to the number of characters copied? Seeing charsWritten to 0 and returning true suggests the input normalized to empty. How is a dev supposed to consume that?
The usage of destination.Slice(0, expected.Length - 1) could potentially lead to an off-by-one error.
destination is already created with the length `expected.Length + 1` so ` destination.Slice(0, expected.Length - 1)` should produce off by one in this code.
This looks like a copy of the above method, just with span instead of string? Can we instead just change the above method to be for span?

Separate from this PR, this method looks ripe for optimizing with SearchValues (or maybe just IndexOfAnyExceptInRange), skipping all characters < '\ud800' quickly.
cc: @MihaZupan

A few other places with a similar idea (`SearchValues` one does have a fast path):

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8fca0a156dcbb1eba5c79e387a6d8f924bfdd3a6/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/SearchValues/Strings/StringSearchValues.cs#L482

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8fca0a156dcbb1eba5c79e387a6d8f924bfdd3a6/src/libraries/System.Private.Xml/src/System/Xml/XmlConvert.cs#L1394

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8fca0a156dcbb1eba5c79e387a6d8f924bfdd3a6/src/libraries/System.Private.Xml/src/System/Xml/XmlCharType.cs#L140

We can address the optimization on this method in another PR as this already existed code and I am just using it. @MihaZupan could you include optimizing this when optimizing the other methods?
